transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I just feel like I don't deserve the trust people put in me. I'm a doctor myself, and lately I just keep replaying these small clinical imperfections in my head, over and over, as if they prove I'm a dangerous doctor.
Aside from these thoughts, how has your overall mood been lately?

Honestly, I'm not entirely sure how to answer that. Um, I guess it's just been pretty low. I haven't really paid much attention to my overall mood outside of... well, outside of just feeling terrible about my work. But yeah, overall, I just feel down, I suppose.
Do you find yourself doing repetitive things, such as checking charts or reviewing patient records over and over, to try to ease that distress?

No, not really. I don't do anything like that. I replay the decisions in my head constantly, but I don't actually go back and keep checking the charts or the patient records. It's more just... well, it's all in my mind. I just sit with the feeling that I did something wrong, but I don't have a physical routine or anything I do to try and make that feeling go away.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities and hobbies you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Um... I used to do a lot, actually. I would plan weekend hikes, go out to take sunrise photos, or cook these big Indonesian dinners for my friends. But for months now, I just haven't had any desire to do any of it. If anything, those things just feel like heavy obligations, and I just can’t seem to make myself care about them anymore.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had stressful times during residency and med school, obviously, but... nothing like this. I've never felt this kind of constant, heavy guilt or just completely lost interest in everything before. This is the first time it's been like this.
Aside from your work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday areas of your life, such as your health, finances, or family?

No, not really. My worries are pretty much entirely focused on work and... well, the mistakes I think I've made there. I don't really worry about my health or money or anything like that. It's just the hospital and my patients that I can't stop thinking about.
How has your sleep been during this time?

My sleep has been pretty bad, honestly. Um... I just have a really hard time staying asleep. I'll wake up at, like, 2 or 3 in the morning, and my mind just starts racing about the hospital and... and everything I've done wrong. Once I'm awake like that, I just can't get back to sleep. So, I'm pretty exhausted during the day.
Given how heavy things have felt, have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Well, I don't have a plan to kill myself or anything like that. But... I do catch myself thinking sometimes that it might just be better if I didn't wake up. Especially after a bad day, you know? Like when I'm just so convinced that I've let my patients down. It just feels like it would be easier.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, first-onset depressive episode characterized by persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia lasting several months, excessive and inappropriate guilt, middle/terminal insomnia, daytime fatigue, and passive suicidal ideation. Compulsive behaviors and generalized anxiety across other life domains were ruled out.

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed mood most of the day
Marked loss of interest and pleasure in previously enjoyed activities (anhedonia)
Excessive, persistent feelings of worthlessness and inappropriate guilt regarding clinical competence
Sleep disturbance with terminal/middle insomnia (waking at 2–3 AM unable to fall back asleep)
Fatigue and exhaustion during the day
Passive suicidal ideation (thinking it might be better not to wake up)

additional_requirements: First episode with no prior history of depressive, hypomanic, or manic episodes
